title: Harmonization of NMR Data Deposition: Adoption of unified NMR data and PDBx/mmCIF
content: News 2026 2025 2024 2023 2022 2021 2020 2019 2018 2017 2016 2015 2014 2013 2012 2011 2010 2009 2008 2007 2006 2005 2004 2003 2002 2001 2000 &nbspPrevious Article Next Article Harmonization of NMR Data Deposition: Adoption of unified NMR data and PDBx/mmCIF 11/17 Since 2020 , wwPDB has distributed unified NMR restraints and chemical shifts data in standard NEF and STAR formats, following recommendations from the NMR Validation Task Forces. This standardization allows for more rigorous validation of restraints within wwPDB validation reports. To assist depositors transitioning to these unified standard formats, wwPDB OneDep deposition system has continued to accept both new unified and software specific formats since its implementation. Starting February 2027 , wwPDB OneDep deposition system will accept NMR experimental data only as a single combined file in STAR (V3) or NEF format and coordinate model file only in PDBx/mmCIF format. All software specific formats for NMR data output from structure determination software and legacy PDB format for coordinate model will be disabled for NMR data depositions. wwPDB continues working with NMR structure determination software developers to support these standard formats. Some structure determination software packages (e.g., Xplor-NIH) already output NMR data in STAR/NEF formats and coordinate models in PDBx/mmCIF. In addition, wwPDB has provided data conversion tools to help depositors and users transition to these standard formats. Depositors with chemical shifts, restraints, or peak lists in software-specific formats should convert them beforehand using bmrb_extract, a standalone NMR data conversion service operated by BMRB and BMRBj: BMRB: https://extract.bmrb.io BMRBj: https://bmrb-extract.pdbj.org This service supports 11 chemical shift formats, 12 restraint formats, and 11 spectral peak list formats, including restraints from XPLOR-NIH, CYANA, CNS, AMBER, and ROSETTA, and peak lists from XEASY, SPARKY, ARIA, and NMRView. Users can upload their coordinate model file in PDB format and existing NMR data files in software specific formats to this service and download a unified NMR data file in NMR-STAR V3 (and NEF) and coordinate file in PDBx/mmCIF for OneDep deposition. As the PDB archive continues to grow, wwPDB will run out of traditional 4-character PDB IDs. Users need to fully adopt PDBx/mmCIF. Beginning July 21, 2027 : New IDs: Only 12-character extended PDB IDs (starting with pdb_ followed by 8 alphanumeric characters, such as pdb_1000axyz) will be issued. File Formats: Structures deposited after July 20, 2027, will only be available in PDBx/mmCIF and PDBML formats. Legacy PDB format files will not be provided for these new entries. Archive Changes and Transition Support: The PDB beta archive will officially replace the main archive. This beta archive and various transition resources are already available to help researchers and developers adapt their workflows. Questions about depositions: deposit-help@mail.wwpdb.org . Questions about bmrb_extract: bmrbhelp@protein.osaka-u.ac.jp .
